title: The Master and Margarita, Bulgakov
subject: litterature
description: The devil visits Stalinist Moscow while a writer recounts Pontius Pilate. Bulgakov claims that manuscripts do not burn.

hero.hook: Satan in Moscow, Pilate in Jerusalem: the novel written in secret under Stalin.

blocks.text: **The Master and Marguerite** was written between **1928** and **1940**, then published in **1967**. It weaves three worlds: Soviet Moscow of the 1930s, ancient Jerusalem and a fantastical space ruled by the devil. **Mikhaïl Bulgakov**, born in **1891** and died in **1940**, conceived it as an artistic testament under the censorship of **Stalin**.

The work affirms that the truth of art ultimately triumphs over political repression, even when the author writes in total clandestinity. His famous phrase, “Manuscripts don’t burn,” has become a symbol of cultural resistance.

sections.title: Bulgakov: writing as an act of resistance

blocks.text: **Mikhaïl Bulgakov**, doctor turned playwright, saw his plays banned from the end of the 1920s. In **1930**, he asked the government for either authorization to emigrate or the right to work. **Stalin** gets him a job at the theater, but his major works remain under lock and key.

blocks.caption: Mikhail Bulgakov, persecuted writer who dictated his novel on his deathbed.

blocks.text: For fear of searches by the , Soviet political police and ancestor of the KGB, Bulgakov burned the first manuscript in **1930**, then began writing again from memory. [[NKVD]]

In **1940**, blind, he dictated the last corrections on his deathbed. The novel would not be published in full until **1967**, twenty-seven years after his death, thanks to the perseverance of his widow.

sections.title: The symphonic structure of the story

blocks.text: In **Moscow**, **Woland**, Satan arrives with his black cat **Behemoth** and sows panic among the corrupt literary caste. At the same time, the **Master** writes the account of **Pontius Pilate** and **Yeshua Ha-Nozri** in Jerusalem. Yeshua is the name given to Jesus in this story. The two stories respond to each other.

blocks.caption: Moscow in the 1930s: the setting for Bulgakov's political satire.

blocks.text: **Daisy** agrees to become a witch and preside over the devil's ball to save the Master, interned after the destruction of his manuscript. His loving sacrifice links the ancient past to the Soviet present. Bulgakov thus weaves three registers: political satire, biblical story and pure fantasy.

sections.title: The metaphysics of cowardice and evil

blocks.text: Bulgakov redefines the devil: Woland reveals that man has not changed despite the promises of . This official artistic doctrine of the USSR required that art serve the party. **cowardice** is “the most terrible of vices”, that of Pilate as well as that of the Soviet critics who betray their colleagues. blocks.text: This sentence states that true ideas survive censorship. The Master is saved because his work is authentic, while his detractors sink into oblivion. Pilate is condemned to wander eternally for having cowardly allowed Yeshua to be executed.

In the USSR, the novel circulated in , clandestine typewritten copies of banned writings. We read it in a low voice among friends. He reintroduced the sacred and the fantastic into a daily life stifled by official ideology. [[Samizdat]]
The novel inspired Mick Jagger to write "Sympathy for the Devil" after Marianne Faithfull offered him an English translation in **1967**.

Marguerite, liberated by love and magic, became an icon of active devotion. Bulgakov fuses black humor and tragedy to question the place of the individual in the face of totalitarian systems. His novel remains one of the most subversive of the 20th century.
Bulgakov wrote this novel in secret to assert that cowardice is the worst sin and that authentic art always survives the flames.
